Nubia

In trying to help with your issue and the additional email sent to me; I wrote this script


library (camtrapR)

# copy your test data - your csv excel recordTable to a new RStudio project (directory)

dir()
# you should have the EXAMPLE.scv file listed.

#  revise your EXAMPLE.csv file. Add a new attribute column and ensure it is in POSIXct format; YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.
#  I did that in Excel adding your date and time columns and customising the format.
# saving as a csv file "EXAMPLE_2.csv"
# copy the new file to this directory

dir() # should have two csv files

# read in revised recordTable
Spp_RT <- read.csv(EXAMPLE_2.csv)
head (Spp_RT)
str(Spp_RT)

# you may have to change the dateTime to POSIXct
#  or it may improve future analysis if the dateTime is a POSIXct not character as at present.

species = "Pan_on",
                                    camOp = FALSE,
                                    output = "binary",
                                    stationCol = "station",
                                    speciesCol = "Short_sp",
                                    recordDateTimeCol = "dateTime",

occasionLength = 7,
                                    occasionStartTime = 6,
                                    day1 = "station",
                                    includeEffort = TRUE,
                                    scaleEffort = TRUE, #because I have stations with 2 cameras
                                    datesAsOccasionNames = FALSE,
                                    timeZone = "America/Mexico_City",
                                    writecsv = TRUE,
                                    outDir = "./"
                                    )


#  the resulting errors - warnings told me that camOP was not available and occasionLength needs attention.

# please reassure me that some of the simpler camtrapR functions that work on a recordTable work with your data before you get to creating a DetHist_rf


David
